regions.region: page 1 title, author block, abstract, and article metadata
regions.finding: Confirmed the true article title and aggregate current-work claim. The page links online Supporting Information, but workspace SI association is unestablished and no SI fact was imported.

regions.region: page 1 introduction and cited prior-work discussion
regions.finding: Prior allene functionalization examples and references are literature context only; external papers were not expanded into experiments of this article.
The proposed copper-catalyzed sp2 C-H cyanation maps to the generic Figure 1C record on page 2 and does not itself define a separate experiment-specific yield.

unresolved: No experiment-specific scale, condition set, or product yield occurs on page 1.

regions.finding: Phomallenic acid B, grasshopper ketone, and enprostil are contextual examples of allene-containing natural products/drugs, not preparations in this paper.
The sp3-HAT and underdeveloped sp2-HAT drawings are generic/prior conceptual reaction classes and are not assigned current-paper yields.
The generic Cu-catalyzed sp2 C-H cyanation is classified as a general scheme; experiment-specific optimization and scope records are separate.

The prose introduces Figure 2A's eight plotted condition screens and reports target 2a versus 2b-2e side-product outcomes. These narrative statements are merged with the matching Figure 2 records on page 3.

unresolved: Figure 1 contains generic R groups and no experiment-specific yield.
Reaction times and yield measurement bases for Figure 2A are not stated.

regions.region: page 3 Figure 2A reaction header, bar chart, structures, and footnotes
regions.finding: Eight independent optimization conditions were retained with CuOAc/L1-L3, NF-1-NF-4 or tBuOOH, TMSCN charges, benzene or tBuOH volumes, Ar/room temperature, separate 2a and 2b-2e yields, and available selectivities. The NF-2 ratio is not numerically labeled and was not calculated.
One metal-free 420 nm experiment gives 4a/4b/4c in 23%/14%/10% with sp2-H:sp3-H selectivity 1:1; it remains one three-product record.

regions.region: page 3 Figure 2C DFT table and transition states
regions.finding: Computed HAT barriers and the 2.16 Å interaction are classified as mechanism/computational evidence, not preparations. The text-reported NF-3/L1/tBuOH 9:1 reference condition is a distinct partial experiment.
The text introduces Figure 3 products 5-8 and their 9:1 to 17:1 selectivity range; the individual experiments are recorded from the complete page-4 figure.

unresolved: The NF-2 red-line selectivity point lacks a printed numerical value.
Figure 2A reaction times/yield bases and Figure 2B scale/time/yield bases are missing.
DFT protocol details are outside the associated workspace evidence.

regions.finding: Nine independent alkyl-allene scope rows were retained with isolated yields, Csp2:Csp3 selectivity, additional C1:C4/C1:C6 values where printed, and NF-5/TMSCN footnote-b overrides for product 13.

Ten independent aryl-allene scope rows were retained. Footnote-b NF-5/TMSCN conditions apply only to 14-17; product 14 lacks a separately printed Csp2:Csp3 value and remains unresolved rather than inferred.
Six heterocycle-containing scope rows were retained. Footnote c creates an ordered second-reagent addition plus an additional 15 h step for 24-26.

Nine complex-molecule scope rows were retained with isolated yields, dr and Csp2:Csp3 selectivity where printed. Separate gram-scale 32 and 38 repeats (1.3 g/77% and 1.43 g/77%) were not merged with the 0.2 mmol rows. Footnote c applies to 37.

unresolved: Figure 3 omits workup, purification, product masses for ordinary rows, and exact systematic identities for many compact structures.
Gram-scale charges/conditions and selectivities are not separately reported.

regions.finding: Two distinct experiments were retained: nBuLi/PhCHO at -95 °C gives 40 (92%), and Cu(CH3CN)4BF4/furan at 50 °C gives 41 (77%, endo:exo 6:1).
The NBS/CH3CN brominating cyclization gives 42 in 66% and dr >20:1. The r.t.-to-40 °C program is an ordered transition with missing duration.
Standard cyanation of 43 to 44 (72%, Csp2:Csp3 7:1) is distinct from the following H2O2/NaOH then CuBr2 sequence to 45. The 61% value is retained as the overall two-operation yield from 44.
DIBAL-H reduction/Wittig conversion of 5 to 46 retains 67% as an overall sequence yield; the separate chiral-phosphine Lu [3+2] cycloaddition of 14 and 47 gives 48 in 75% and 86% ee.

regions.region: page 5 discussion of Figure 3 scope and gram-scale applications
regions.finding: Narrative descriptions of products 5-38 are linked to the page-4 scope and gram-scale records rather than duplicated.

unresolved: Figure 4 omits most quantities, reaction times, workups, purifications, masses, and analytical bases.
Wittig reagent identity is not specified.
The two multi-operation yields cannot be assigned to their final steps alone.

regions.region: page 6 upper-left continuation of Figure 4 discussion
regions.finding: The prose confirms 46 as a sequential nitrile-reduction/Wittig product and 48 as a 75%/86% ee asymmetric [3+2] product; these update the page-5 arrows and do not create duplicate reactions.

regions.region: page 6 Figure 5 shared conditions and products 49-51
regions.finding: Three distinct enantioselective cyanation experiments were retained under CuOAc/Box L4, NF-6/TMSCN, C6F6/PhCF3 9:1, Ar, -8 °C: 49 (54%, 88% ee), 50 (62%, 92% ee), and 51 (68%, 37% ee).
